daniyal:
Create an ORIGINAL character for Rad-e Hoor / The Solar Trace, a first-person audio-survival PC game set in a fictional canyon in Iran's Lut Desert. Use grounded adult proportions and contemporary everyday Iranian workwear. The visual language is stylized 3D volume with selective ink contours, restrained surface-attached hatching and subtle print texture; material color remains readable and anatomy remains functional. Do not imitate a recognizable existing fictional character, actor or branded costume. No photoreal beauty advertising, chibi anatomy, superhero proportions, costume orientalist fantasy, religious symbols or tattoos. Do not add weapons, skull symbols, invented text or plot-signaling magical markings. Neutral material and face presentation must not encode moral worth through appearance.

SUBJECT: CH01, Daniyal. Design proportions: 38 years; 183 cm; 81 kg.
BODY / FACE: A working mechanic and off-road driver, strong forearms, ordinary waist, proportionate thighs, natural shoulders; not a bodybuilder. Warm dark wheat-brown skin with sun exposure on forehead and forearms. Squared jaw, prominent cheekbones, subtly deviated nose, dark hazel eyes with slightly heavy lids. Short wavy black hair, limited gray at temples, five-to-seven-day stubble. A small old stitched scar on the right eyebrow, an old four-centimeter battery burn on the LEFT forearm, callused hands and old knuckle cuts. The right shoulder rests very slightly lower; do not exaggerate it.
CLOTHING / PROPS: Khaki cotton T-shirt, olive work shirt with repaired elbows, thin work vest, camel-colored trousers with a LEFT-knee patch, worn unbranded suede work boots. Baseline is day workwear with NO night jacket or hat on the head; a short brown windbreaker and simple short-brim cloth cap are separate approved variants. A compact frequency meter fastens to the LEFT forearm, chest light on the RIGHT, closed wrench sheath on RIGHT thigh; pen and paper inside the LEFT inner pocket. Hand-touch baseline has bare hands; work gloves are separate loading-only props. No loose metal, towing strap draped across the torso, or tool belt full of invented equipment.
PERFORMANCE INTENT: Precise with a mechanical uncertainty, evasive when a difficult human question arrives. Show a useful hand that can pause before taking over another person's task. A neutral baseline can look relaxed; do not make him permanently ashamed or angry. Later growth is sharing information, asking for a clear signal and accepting help.
STATE AND CONTINUITY: Baseline uninjured; retain old marks. Chapter 5 RIGHT sleeve scratch exists only after shield contact. Chapter 9 RIGHT hand cut and subsequent bandage are separate later variants. Never age him across seven entries.

OUTPUT: one full-body character, FRONT three-quarter view with near-orthographic proportions, entire head/hands/feet in frame, simple warm-gray background, diffuse even studio illumination, clear material boundaries, relaxed neutral A-pose with separated arms and legs, bare visible hands unless clothing above requires otherwise. No cinematic scenery, dramatic cast shadow, text labels, contact sheet, duplicate person, alternate costume in the same image or props obscuring anatomy. Keep all attachment points plausible. This is a single-subject visual reference, not a delivered mesh or proof of rig quality.

canyon_day:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: widescreen environment concept for an original native 3D PC game, Rad-e Hoor / The Solar Trace.
Primary request: a beautiful, believable and playable canyon background during the DAY-ONE DELIVERY, before the supernatural night. Single wide landscape image.
Scene: a fictional deep twisting canyon in Iran's Lut Desert. Very tall sedimentary walls, broad visible layers of pale sand, warm brick-red silt and muted gray clay, occasional narrow gypsum/salt seams reflecting sunlight naturally. A dry winding drivable floor, natural S-bend hiding the next stretch; distinct sandy vehicle line and modest walkable margins. Strong readable foreground, middle-ground bend, and high distant wall. No uniform identical pillars or volcanic basalt.
View: first-person human eye-level from the approach, natural perspective, wide horizontal composition. A SMALL unbranded practical older off-road vehicle, structurally intact, can provide scale in the middle distance; it is not a wreck. It must be dwarfed by the canyon walls without blocking the whole route. Keep road widths visually usable by this vehicle.
Mood and light: calm genuine late-afternoon desert beauty before fear; soft warm sunlight on upper strata, cool open shade near the floor, clear but restrained palette, thin strip of sky. A few sparse small shrubs in protected shade and very limited tiny signs of ordinary life; not a lush oasis and not a lifeless horror ruin.
Style: original grounded stylized 3D environment with sculptural volume, selective ink edgework, surface-attached fine hatching and restrained print texture. Elegant game concept art, not a travel photograph, not an existing game's screenshot.
Materials: fine granular sediment, brittle layered ledges, practical tire marks that follow a physical path; natural unlit crystalline reflections. No glowing amber veins during day, no religion, no runes, no magical ruins, no temple, no gates or objects added as plot symbols. No river, freshwater spring, greenery oasis, lava, giant monster, person, text, logo, HUD, compass, diagram arrows or watermark. This is an environment visual proposal, not an accurate mapped real-world canyon or a verified navigation layout. Preserve physical route readability and make the setting inviting enough that its later transformation matters.
caravanserai_night:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: wide horizontal environment concept for Rad-e Hoor, an original first-person audio-survival native PC game.
Primary request: a tense yet navigable nighttime background of a FICTIONAL brick caravanserai courtyard inside the deep sedimentary canyon. This is chapter 5, not the real Shafiabad caravanserai.
Layout composition: human eye-level from the safe parking corner. A structurally intact plain older off-road vehicle sits under a sound wall in the near right foreground, a readable open sandy route crosses the courtyard, a narrow stone-framed side passage leads toward a small old field transmitter on a practical metal stand. Small solar/battery equipment belongs to the field team, not a futuristic generator. Keep transmitter visibly distinct from the vehicle. A sheltered shallow vestibule and a separate CLOSED service-store gate are visible in the left midground; gate is a physical sliding mechanism, no magical sealed boss door. The inner slow-time chamber is NOT an extra open exit. Wall/arch arrangement must leave a plausible pedestrian route and return to the car.
Background: high layered sedimentary canyon walls dwarf the modest weathered brick building. Flat dry sand floor interrupted by modest stone thresholds; no freshwater stream, lush greenery or volcanic rock.
Light/mood: restrained low moonlight from the strip of sky and one low-power practical work lamp; blue-gray open shadow, desaturated earth/clay and very sparse dim amber light at tiny stone seams only, not neon seams covering every wall. The floor and stone passage edges remain readable. Unease comes from occlusion, distance and a mundane workspace after people have gone, not total darkness or gore.
Visual style: original stylized 3D volume, selective ink contours and surface-attached fine hatching with restrained print texture. Functional contemporary expedition props against repaired masonry; believable scale and clean spatial layers. A polished environment concept with foreground/midground/background; not a travel photo, not an existing game screenshot.
Avoid: people, creatures, statues, graveyard, palace, mosque, religious symbols, inscriptions, fantasy runes, glowing crystals the size of buildings, weapons, human remains, torch-lit medieval dungeon, HUD, text, diagram arrows, logos or watermark. No object should erase the open return route. This is an atmospheric visual concept; it does not certify acoustic safety, distances or a Unity level.
